study.title: The Brain Effects of Laser Acupuncture in Healthy Individuals: An fMRI Investigation
study.study_design: within-subject blocked fMRI design with randomized stimulation order
study.randomization: 4 acupoints stimulated twice in random order; control point stimulated once per subject
study.blinding: subjects blinded to verum vs placebo (laser off) stimulation due to absence of skin sensation from low-intensity laser
study.population: healthy volunteers aged 18-50 years recruited from staff and students of the University of New South Wales and Prince of Wales Hospital, Sydney, Australia
study.disease_condition: healthy individuals (no depression or psychiatric disorder)
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handed, aged 18-50 years, no past history of depression or other psychiatric disorder, Beck Depression Inventory score <10, no history of drug or alcohol abuse, no medication intake within 3 months of the study, no neurological or systemic disorders
study.exclusion_criteria: any contra-indications to MRI (pacemaker, ferromagnetic implants or foreign body, claustrophobia); history of depression or psychiatric disorder; BDI score >=10; drug or alcohol abuse; medication within 3 months; neurological or systemic disorders

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Described as non-penetrating laser held with light touch on skin surface. No skin breaking occurs; device makes surface contact only. This is Level 3 regardless of the 'verum' label, as the physical tissue engagement is purely at the skin surface with no penetration.

conditions.timepoint_exact: during scanning session; alternating rest blocks within block design
conditions.scan_context: placebo condition during rest phases of block design; laser switched off
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The laser device is switched off during this condition. Although the device is held with light touch on the skin surface, the condition is explicitly described as a 'rest' phase with laser off, and the sham subtype is 'placebo laser (laser off)'. Physically, no energy is delivered and the primary defining feature of this condition is no active stimulation. However, the device does physically touch the skin. Strictly by physical contact, this would be Level 3 (surface contact). But the condition is classified as 'rest' and the laser is off with no therapeutic contact intended. Given the device is still held on the skin, Level 3 is the most accurate physical depth classification — surface contact, no penetration, no energy delivery.

contrasts._sham_description: A control non-acupoint (sham point) located on the abdominal surface, midway between SP15 (four cun from the umbilicus) and ST25 (two cun from the umbilicus), away from the abdominal meridians. Stimulated with the same fibreoptic infrared laser (808 nm, 25 mW) as the verum acupoints, in the same block design (20-second on/off blocks). The sham condition was compared against all other points (verum laser per point > all others), not against rest alone; however the placebo (laser off) condition served as the rest/baseline within the block design.

extraction_notes.note: No trial registration number is reported in the paper.
PMID is not reported in the paper text; only the DOI (10.1371/journal.pone.0012619) is provided.

The p_value column in Table 1 is listed as '0' for all entries. This likely represents p<0.001 (truncated display) but the exact values are not provided. Extracted as '0' to faithfully reflect the table.

The paper states CV14 had 'no significant deactivation in the grey matter' and HT7 had 'no significant activation or deactivation.' These null results are captured in narrative-only contrast entries with empty coordinate arrays.

The contrast design is described as 'verum laser per point > all others' and 'all others > verum laser per point' at the group level. This is not a simple verum vs. placebo contrast; each acupoint is contrasted against all other acupoints and the control point combined. This is preserved as described.

The paper reports LR14 activations in the text as 'contralateral frontal cortex' and parietal but the table labels these as 'Left' without explicit reference to laterality of stimulus. The paper states LR14 was stimulated on the right side (Figure 1 caption: 'right LR14'), making these activations contralateral. The table entries are extracted as reported (Left hemisphere).

The paper reports LR8 deactivation as 'bilateral frontal cortices (middle frontal gyrus), (contralateral superior frontal gyrus)' in the text. In the table, two middle frontal gyrus entries are shown (Right and Left), consistent with bilateral. The text also notes 'bilateral middle frontal gyrus deactivation' for LR8 in the laterality section. All table entries have been extracted.

No t-statistics, F-statistics, or exact p-values beyond the threshold criterion (p<0.001, 15 contiguous voxels) are reported for any neuroimaging contrast. The table p_vox column shows '0' for all entries.

No formal deqi measurement instrument (e.g., MGQ, MASS, VAS for deqi) was administered. The paper explicitly states low-intensity laser produces no skin sensation and subjects were blinded to on/off phases.
No expectancy or credibility instrument (e.g., Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire) was administered or reported.
No motion exclusion criteria or motion parameter thresholds are specified beyond spatial realignment to the first volume. Head motion exclusion criteria are not reported.
Global signal regression is not mentioned in the preprocessing or analysis methods.

The Spielberger State Anxiety Inventory post-imaging ratings are described as 'selected items' only, not the full scale score. Individual items were extracted as separate outcome entries. No statistical comparisons between conditions or timepoints are reported for these ratings.

The coordinate table in the paper uses the label 'pvox' with value '0' for all entries. This may represent rounded p-values at the voxel level below the threshold rather than true zero; extracted verbatim as '0'.
The paper uses SPM2 and MNI normalization. Coordinate space is reported as MNI in the methods. No Talairach conversion is mentioned.

The paper describes the control point as being on the 'right' side (Figure 1 label: 'control pt right'), and the postcentral gyrus activation is 'Right Postcentral Gyrus' (contralateral to the left side where it is not stimulated, or ipsilateral to the right control point). The laterality interpretation in the text and figure is preserved as extracted.
The 'No of Voxels' column in Table 1 is described as cluster size but no voxel volume or mm3 conversion is reported. Cluster extent unit is extracted as 'voxels'.
The paper states HT7 showed no significant activation or deactivation. This is a reported null result and has been preserved as a narrative-only entry in neural results.

The Beck Depression Inventory reference [21] in the participants section appears to cite 'Rindge D (2009) Lasers and De Qi' which is likely a citation numbering error in the paper. This is noted but extracted as reported.

The paper states 'nine runs per subject' in total. With 4 acupoints stimulated twice (8 runs) and the control point once (1 run), this totals 9 runs, consistent with the description. Session duration per run is not explicitly given in minutes.
Sham>rest re-extraction: added 2 contrasts, 2 peaks
